2609.01352.title: CHARM: Character Hallucination for Multicultural Role Play Benchmark
2609.01352.paper_summary: Role-playing large language models (LLMs) are expected to adopt a character's style while also respecting that character's knowledge boundaries. Prior evaluations detect character hallucination but rarely distinguish whether errors arise from failure to recognize a boundary or from failure to comply despite recognition. We introduce CHARM, a multicultural benchmark of 40 real and fictional characters drawn from five cultural-linguistic regions, and validated by native reviewers. It probes two boundary types, Temporal (historical vs. modern) and Cross-Universe (entities outside a character's narrative or historical universe), using abstention-enabled multiple-choice questions. We propose a two-stage evaluation that separates Boundary-Awareness (explicit recognition that a query is out of scope) from Boundary-Compliance (abstention when answering concrete questions). Evaluations across six LLMs show that hallucination is driven predominantly by compliance failures. Models frequently acknowledge that a query lies outside the character's knowledge yet still provide factual, out-of-character answers. By re-posing the same questions to the target character, we confirm that a large fraction of these cases are verified parametric overrides; the model stores the relevant fact but fails to suppress it. We also observe systematic cultural variation in these failures, consistent with imbalances in how characters from different regions are represented in model knowledge.
2609.01352.paper_summary_zh: 角色扮演的大型語言模型（LLMs）預期會採用角色的風格，同時尊重該角色的知識邊界。<lb/>先前的評估檢測到角色幻覺，但很少區分錯誤是由於未能識別邊界還是儘管識別卻未能遵守。<lb/>我們介紹了CHARM，一個涵蓋來自五個文化語言區域的40個真實和虛構角色的多文化基準，並由母語審核員驗證。<lb/>它探討了兩種邊界類型：時間性（歷史 vs. 現代）和跨宇宙（角色敘事或歷史宇宙之外的實體），使用啟用放棄的多選問題。<lb/>我們提出了一個兩階段的評估，將邊界意識（明確識別查詢超出範疇）與邊界遵守（在回答具體問題時的放棄）分開。<lb/>在六個LLMs的評估中顯示，幻覺主要是由遵守失敗驅動的。<lb/>模型經常承認查詢超出了角色的知識範疇，但仍然提供事實性的、非角色的答案。<lb/>通過將相同的問題重新提問給目標角色，我們確認這些案例中有很大一部分是經過驗證的參數覆蓋；模型儲存了相關事實，但未能抑制它。<lb/>我們還觀察到這些失敗中存在系統性的文化變異，與不同地區角色在模型知識中的表現不平衡一致。
